methodology.title: The rules are part of the result.
methodology.intro: A model’s score only means something when you know how it played.
methodology.legalBody: The rules engine accepts legal UCI moves. Illegal, unparseable and cut-off attempts stay in the timeline with the end of the model’s reply; they never move a piece, and a reply cut off at its output limit never counts as a move. The configured attempt allowance determines forfeits.
methodology.contextBody: Fresh-context turns receive the current position, side to move, draw information, rules and remaining allowance. Persistent turns retain that player’s conversation. Neither player sees the other’s private conversation.
methodology.identityBody: Anonymous games omit the opponent’s configured model identity. Commentary can be enabled independently, so it may reveal identity clues. Revealed games name the opponent; neither mode guarantees that a model cannot guess identity.
methodology.budgetBody: Every dispatch reserves a conservative token and cost allowance, including transport retries, before inference. There is no fixed reply cap: each reply may use the model’s own maximum output, limited by what the side’s budgets can still pay, unless the ruleset sets one for an experiment. Reported usage and price-based cost estimates are separate from reservations. Missing provider usage is not proof of zero cost.
methodology.rankBody: Standings separate exact rulesets and wire protocols. Imported games are local experiments, never automatic evidence of model identity. Small samples remain provisional. Chess performance is not a general intelligence score.
methodology.privacyBody: Local inference credentials stay in your local process. Portable game archives contain game data, not provider credentials. Public viewers trigger no inference calls.

identity.hidden: Neither side is told which model it is playing.
identity.disclosed: Each side is told its opponent's name and model id.

context.fresh: Every move is a new conversation that sees only the current position.
context.persistent: Each side keeps one conversation for the whole game, with its earlier moves.

tools.hidden: The model gets the board only and must find a legal move itself.
tools.tool: The model can call a tool that lists the legal moves.
tools.provided: Every prompt lists the legal moves.

moveFormat.strict: The reply must be the exact JSON move; anything else is a rejected attempt.
moveFormat.lenient: Also reads a JSON move inside prose and converts legal SAN to UCI. Ranked separately.

engine.off: No Stockfish for the players. Spectators still see an evaluation bar, scored separately.
engine.tool: Models may ask Stockfish about the position, at most 2 calls per turn.
engine.after-move: Stockfish scores the position after every move, and the players see the score.
engine.both: The engine tool plus a score after every move that the players see.

accounting.provider: Tokens are counted from what the provider reports, reserved before each request.
accounting.cl100k_base: Every model is counted with one tokenizer (cl100k_base), so allowances are comparable.

explain.tokenBudget: Total tokens each player may use in the game ({{min}} to {{max}}).
explain.budget: The most each player may spend, in US dollars ({{min}} to {{max}}).
explain.plies: The game ends as a draw after this many half-moves ({{min}} to {{max}}).

remarks.commentary: Each player may add one short, neutral remark about its own move or plan.
remarks.trash-talk: Models may trash talk and choose their own tone from move to move: playful, friendly, gracious, neutral or silent. Remarks stay tasteful and about the game, with no slurs, profanity or remarks about anyone's identity.

explain.moveLimit: A safety limit for one move. Blank uses {{auto}}: one minute, never longer than a side's clock. {{min}}–{{max}} seconds.

illegalPolicy.forfeit: After this many rejected moves on one turn, that side loses the game.
illegalPolicy.retry: No forfeit: the side keeps trying until it plays a legal move, and every rejected move is recorded. The per-move limit, the clock and the side's token and spend budgets still apply and end the game when one runs out.

explain.maxAttempts: Rejected moves allowed on one turn ({{min}} to {{max}}).
explain.replyCap: Off by default: each reply may use the model's own maximum output (White {{white}}, Black {{black}} tokens), limited by what its budgets can still pay. Set a cap ({{min}} to {{max}}) only for experiments: hidden reasoning counts against it on many providers, and a reply cut off at it is rejected as out of space. A cap is part of the rules, so capped games rank separately.
